[2026-09-03 · manual_entry] The workshop lights started flickering in the evenings.
[2026-09-05 · manual_entry] A new kiln was installed on the same circuit as the lights.
[2026-09-06 · manual_entry] The flickering continues most evenings.
[2026-09-08 · manual_entry] The utility reported voltage sags on our street twice this month.

What's causing the flickering?
cases.X: The kiln is the prime suspect. The flickering started before it arrived, but a new kiln on the same circuit is a heavy intermittent load, and 'most evenings' is exactly when a kiln cycles and when everyone's home drawing power. The utility's voltage sags are a real alternative — twice in a month is a pattern — but sags would likely affect the whole street's houses, not just your lights, and the timing lines up better with a local load. What's probably happening: the kiln's draw is dipping voltage on your shared circuit. Next step: note whether flickering coincides with the kiln firing, and try running the lights on a different circuit for a few evenings to confirm. If it persists off-circuit, it's the utility's problem to fix.

The bigger issue is measurement cadence — you're running the business on a nine-month-old number. Reinstitute quarterly measurement, and interview the two at-risk clients now if you haven't; whatever the exact rate, it's higher than 4% until proven otherwise.
